notes: The progress bar told you nothing, so it stopped pretending. It was filling against the give-up deadline rather than the work — and because a confirmed cold start earns more time, it slid backwards whenever the wait was going well. Nothing in the pipeline reports how far through a picture is, so the bar is now simply a moving marker meaning 'still running', and the caption above it carries the real state, read live from RunPod: booting and loading the model, ready and starting, queued with the number of jobs ahead of yours, throttled and waiting on a GPU, or actually painting. Photo generation gets that narration for the first time — it was the longer wait of the two and had only the words 'painting the photo' for it. When a job finishes, the log records how long it sat in the queue and how long the GPU actually worked, which is the number that explains a slow photo.
